about: The scripted AI lesson for g5-development (2026-11-19, Phase B, brief docs/briefs/2026-11-15-script-four-topics.md): every word she sees is written here once and checked (tools/check-script.js, tools/review-lesson.js --script). The AI only marks her typed answers (choosing a branch written here), answers her own questions, and sorts her messages. It opens with two questions on averages, which the exam's data questions use.

keyPoints.heading: What is development and how do we measure it?

steps.text: Welcome! This lesson is about why some countries are much richer and healthier than others, how we measure the difference, and what people do to close it.

steps.question: First, two quick maths questions you will need. Four friends have £2, £4, £6 and £8. What is the mean amount?
steps.right: Yes: add them up (£20) and share by 4: £5 each.

wrong.other: Not quite: £5. Add them up to £20, then divide by 4.
wrong.total: Nearly: £20 is the total. The mean shares it out: £20 ÷ 4 = £5.
wrong.mid: Not quite: the mean is the total shared out equally: £20 ÷ 4 = £5.

idk.hint: Add the four amounts, then divide by how many friends there are.

steps.answerWhy: The mean is the total shared out equally: £20 ÷ 4 = £5.

steps.question: Second: what is the range of £2, £4, £6 and £8?
steps.right: Yes: the highest minus the lowest, £8 − £2 = £6.

wrong.other: Not quite: £6, the highest minus the lowest.
wrong.mean: Not quite: £5 is the mean. The range is the highest minus the lowest: £8 − £2 = £6.
wrong.max: Not quite: £8 is the highest. The range is the highest minus the lowest: £8 − £2 = £6.

idk.hint: Take the smallest amount away from the biggest.

steps.answerWhy: The range is the highest minus the lowest: £8 − £2 = £6.

steps.text: Now this lesson. Development means people's quality of life getting better: richer, healthier and better educated. To compare countries, geographers use measures.
The main money measure is GNI per head: all the income a country earns in a year, shared out equally between its people. It is a mean income for each person.

steps.question: In 2025, GNI per head was about $54,550 in the UK and $1,360 in Nigeria. Roughly how many times richer, per person, was the UK?
steps.right: Yes: 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40. That gap is what this lesson is about.

wrong.other: Not quite: about 40 times. 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40.
wrong.four: Not quite: 4 × 1,360 is only about 5,440. 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40.
wrong.four100: Not quite: 400 × 1,360 would be over half a million. 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40.

idk.hint: Divide 54,550 by 1,360. Is the answer nearer 4, 40 or 400?

steps.answerWhy: 54,550 ÷ 1,360 is about 40, so the UK earned about 40 times more per person.

steps.text: Social measures are about people's lives. Life expectancy is how long a baby born now can expect to live: about 84 years in Japan and 55 in Nigeria.
The infant mortality rate is how many babies, in every 1,000 born alive, die before their first birthday, each year. In Japan it is about 2; in Nigeria about 70.

steps.question: An exam asks: "What is meant by infant mortality rate?" Which answer scores both marks?

options.text: The number of babies per 1,000 born alive who die before age 1, each year
The number of babies who die

steps.right: Yes: it needs the "per 1,000" and the "before their first birthday", each year.

wrong.other: Not quite: babies per 1,000 born alive who die before age 1, each year.
wrong.total: Nearly: a rate is not a total. It is per 1,000 babies born alive, each year, dying before their first birthday.
wrong.life: Not quite: that sounds like life expectancy. Infant mortality is babies per 1,000 born alive who die before age 1, each year.

idk.hint: A rate is always "per" something. Which option says per 1,000?

steps.answerWhy: Infant mortality rate: the number of babies, per 1,000 born alive, who die before their first birthday, each year.

steps.text: Other social measures are people per doctor, the share of adults who can read and write, and access to safe water.
The HDI, or Human Development Index, combines three things into one score between 0 and 1: income, life expectancy and education.
Every measure has a limitation: a reason it can mislead. GNI per head is a mean, so a few very rich people can hide many poor ones.

steps.question: Which is a limitation of GNI per head?

options.text: It is an average, so it hides how unequally money is shared
It does not show life expectancy

steps.right: Yes: that is why it can mislead. A limitation says why a measure gives a false picture.

wrong.other: Not quite: it is an average, so it hides how unequally money is shared.
wrong.notshow: True, but examiners want why it can mislead, not what it leaves out. It is an average, so it hides how unequally money is shared.
wrong.dollars: Not quite: dollars let countries be compared fairly. The problem is that it is an average, so it hides inequality.

idk.hint: Think of the mean of £1, £1, £1 and £97. Does £25 describe most people?

steps.answerWhy: GNI per head is an average, so it hides how unequally money is shared: a limitation.

steps.prompt: In one line: what is the HDI made from?
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: the HDI combines income, life expectancy and education into one score.

steps.text: The World Bank, an international organisation that lends money for development, sorts countries into groups by GNI per head.
A rich country, such as the UK or Japan, is called an HIC: a high income country.
One of the poorest countries, such as Niger or Malawi, is called an LIC: a low income country.
In between are middle income countries. Kenya is one: lower-middle income, still a poorer country.
A country whose economy has started to grow fast as it builds up industry is called an NEE: a newly emerging economy. China, India, Brazil and Nigeria are NEEs.

steps.question: Niger has a GNI per head of about $750. Which group is it in?
steps.right: Yes: one of the poorest countries, an LIC.

wrong.other: Not quite: an LIC, a low income country.
wrong.hic: Not quite: $750 a year is very low. Niger is an LIC.
wrong.nee: Not quite: Niger's economy is not growing fast through industry. It is an LIC.

idk.hint: Is $750 a year high or low for a whole year's income?

steps.answerWhy: With about $750 per person, Niger is one of the poorest countries: an LIC.

steps.text: An older way of splitting the world is the Brandt Line: a line on a world map dividing a richer "North" from a poorer "South". It fits today badly, because fast-growing countries such as China sit in the "South".

steps.prompt: In one line: what is an NEE?
points: a country whose economy has started to grow fast as it builds up industry
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: an NEE is a newly emerging economy, growing fast as it builds up industry.

keyPoints.heading: Population and development: the Demographic Transition Model

steps.text: As a country develops, its births and deaths change in a pattern. The birth rate is the number of babies born for every 1,000 people each year.
The death rate is the number of people who die for every 1,000 people each year.
The Demographic Transition Model, or DTM, shows how the two rates change over five stages as a country develops.
Stage 1: both rates are high, so the population stays small. Stage 2: the death rate falls fast, as clean water, food and health care improve, but births stay high. The population grows fast.

steps.question: Predict: in stage 2, what happens to the size of the population?
steps.right: Yes: many more people are born than die, so it grows fast. Many LICs are in stage 2.

wrong.other: Not quite: it grows fast, because many more are born than die.
wrong.shrink: Not quite: births are still high and deaths are low, so far more people are born than die. It grows fast.
wrong.same: Not quite: births are now much higher than deaths, so the population grows fast.

idk.hint: Are more people being born, or dying?

steps.answerWhy: Births stay high while deaths fall, so far more people are born than die: the population grows fast.

steps.text: Stage 3: the birth rate falls too, as fewer babies die, more girls go to school and more women go out to work. Many NEEs are here.
Stage 4: both rates are low, so the population is steady. Most HICs, such as the UK, are here. Stage 5: births fall below deaths and the population slowly shrinks, as in Japan.

steps.question: Why might moving into stage 3 help a country's economy?

options.text: With fewer children to look after, more women can go out to work

steps.right: Yes: more people working means more money earned and more tax collected.

wrong.other: Not quite: with fewer children to look after, more women can work.
wrong.more: Not quite: in stage 3 the birth rate falls. With fewer children to look after, more women can work.
wrong.death: Not quite: the death rate stays low. The change is fewer births, so more women can work.

idk.hint: In stage 3 the birth rate falls. How does that change family life?

steps.answerWhy: With fewer children to look after, more women can go out to work, which helps the economy.

steps.prompt: In one line: which DTM stage are many LICs in, and why does their population grow fast?
points: the death rate has fallen but the birth rate is still high
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: many LICs are in stage 2, where the death rate has fallen but the birth rate is still high.

steps.text: Development is uneven: some countries are far ahead of others. The difference between the richest and poorest countries is called the development gap.

The causes of the gap come in three groups. Physical causes come from nature: being landlocked, with no coastline, makes trade costly; drought, poor soils, natural hazards and diseases such as malaria hold people back.

steps.question: Which of these is a physical cause of uneven development?
steps.right: Yes: drought comes from nature, so it is physical.

wrong.other: Not quite: frequent droughts. Physical means it comes from nature.
wrong.debt: Not quite: debt is about money, an economic cause. Physical means from nature, like drought.
wrong.borders: Not quite: borders drawn by rulers come from history. Physical means from nature, like drought.

idk.hint: Physical means it comes from nature. Which option is the weather?

steps.answerWhy: Drought comes from nature, so it is a physical cause.

steps.text: Economic causes come from trade and money. Raw materials, such as coffee or copper, are called primary products: they earn little and their prices swing up and down, while poorer countries must buy costly manufactured goods.

Historical causes come from the past. Colonialism is when one country rules another for its own benefit: European countries ruled much of Africa and Asia, took raw materials and drew borders that split peoples.
Uneven development has consequences. There are big differences, called disparities, in wealth and in health between countries.
Uneven development also causes international migration: people moving to live in another country, often from poorer countries to richer ones for work, higher pay and safety. Many send money home.

steps.question: Why does uneven development cause international migration?

options.text: People move to richer countries for jobs and higher pay

steps.right: Yes: the gap in jobs and pay pulls people to richer countries.

wrong.other: Not quite: people move to richer countries for jobs and higher pay.
wrong.weather: Not quite: the weather is not the reason. People move for jobs and higher pay.
wrong.nopeople: Not quite: poorer countries have many people. They move to richer countries for jobs and higher pay.

idk.hint: If wages in one country are many times higher, what might some people do?

steps.answerWhy: People move from poorer to richer countries for jobs, higher pay and safety.

steps.prompt: In one line: name the three groups of causes of uneven development.
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: the causes are physical, economic and historical.

keyPoints.heading: Strategies to reduce the development gap

steps.text: Several strategies try to close the gap. Investment means companies or other countries putting money into businesses, roads and factories; industrial development then creates jobs and taxes.
Aid is help from one country or charity to another: money, goods or skills, given or lent on very easy terms. It can save lives, but it can be wasted.
Debt relief cancels some of the money a poor country owes, so money paid out as interest can go on health and schools instead. Most of the 39 countries that qualified for one scheme have been helped.

steps.question: A student writes: "Debt relief is a loan to help a poor country." What is wrong?

options.text: Debt relief cancels money owed; it is not a new loan
Nothing: debt relief is a loan
Debt relief is only for rich countries

steps.right: Yes: debt relief cancels debt. Mixing it up with loans is a common exam mistake.

wrong.other: Not quite: debt relief cancels money owed; it is not a new loan.
wrong.loan: Not quite: a loan adds debt. Debt relief takes debt away.
wrong.rich: Not quite: it is for poor countries. And it cancels money owed; it is not a loan.

idk.hint: Does debt relief add to what the country owes, or take some away?

steps.answerWhy: Debt relief cancels money a poor country owes; it is not a loan.

steps.text: Microfinance means very small loans to people too poor to use an ordinary bank, to start a small business. Grameen Bank in Bangladesh lends mostly to women.
Intermediate technology is simple equipment local people can make, use and mend, such as a hand water pump.
Fairtrade pays farmers a fair minimum price for their crop, plus extra money for their community.
Tourism brings money and jobs. In Kenya, international tourists grew from about 1.2 million in 2015 to about 2 million in 2019, for safaris and beaches.
In 2019 Kenya's tourism earned $1.76 billion, about 15% of what Kenya earns from selling abroad. That money pays wages, taxes and new roads.

steps.question: Which is a weakness of tourism as a way to close the gap?

options.text: Some of the money goes to foreign hotel companies
It brings no jobs at all

steps.right: Yes: money leaking abroad means less stays in Kenya. Tourists also stay away after terrorism or a pandemic.

wrong.other: Not quite: some of the money goes to foreign hotel companies.
wrong.nojobs: Not quite: tourism does bring jobs. Its weakness is that some money goes to foreign companies.
wrong.rich: Not quite: it helps poorer countries like Kenya, but some money leaks to foreign companies.

idk.hint: Who owns many big hotels? Where does their profit go?

steps.answerWhy: Some of the money goes to foreign hotel companies, and visitor numbers fall after terrorism or a pandemic.

steps.prompt: In one line: what is the difference between debt relief and microfinance?
points: debt relief cancels money a country owes
microfinance is a small loan to a person
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: debt relief cancels money a country owes, while microfinance is a small loan to a person.

steps.text: The picture is mixed. Some NEEs, especially China and India, have grown fast, and hundreds of millions of their people now have higher incomes.
Extreme poverty means living on less than $3 a day. The share of the world's people in extreme poverty fell from about 43% in 1990 to about 10% in 2024.

steps.question: Which piece of evidence shows the gap is NOT closing everywhere?

options.text: Many of the poorest African countries are falling further behind
Extreme poverty fell from about 43% to 10%
China and India have grown fast

steps.right: Yes: progress is uneven, so for many of the poorest countries the gap is widening.

wrong.other: Not quite: many of the poorest African countries are falling further behind.
wrong.falling: Not quite: that shows progress. The evidence against is that many of the poorest African countries are falling behind.
wrong.china: Not quite: that shows the gap closing for some. Many of the poorest African countries are falling behind.

idk.hint: Two options show progress. Which one shows some countries falling behind?

steps.answerWhy: Many of the poorest countries, especially in Africa, are falling further behind, so the gap is not closing everywhere.

steps.text: The United Nations has set Sustainable Development Goals: targets for every country to end poverty and hunger and improve health and schooling.

steps.prompt: In one line: is the development gap closing? Give one point each way.
points: closing for some (fast-growing NEEs; less extreme poverty)
not for many of the poorest countries
steps.idk: No problem. A good line would be: it is closing for fast-growing countries such as China, but many of the poorest African countries are falling behind.

steps.text: Now for a short quiz: six questions on the whole lesson. Take your time.

steps.question: Quiz, question 1 of 6: what does the HDI combine?
steps.right: Yes: income, life expectancy and education.

wrong.other: Not quite: income, life expectancy and education.
wrong.w1: Not quite: income alone is GNI per head. The HDI adds life expectancy and education.
wrong.w2: Not quite: the HDI combines income, life expectancy and education.

steps.answerWhy: The HDI combines income, life expectancy and education.

steps.question: Quiz, question 2 of 6: the birth rate is the number of babies born…?

wrong.other: Not quite: for every 1,000 people each year.
wrong.w1: Not quite: a rate is not a total. It is per 1,000 people each year.
wrong.w2: Not quite: the birth rate is per 1,000 people each year.

steps.answerWhy: The birth rate is births for every 1,000 people each year.

steps.question: Quiz, question 3 of 6: which DTM stage are most HICs, such as the UK, in?
steps.right: Yes: stage 4, with low birth and death rates.

wrong.w1: Not quite: stage 2 has a high birth rate; many LICs are there. Most HICs are in stage 4.
wrong.w2: Not quite: stage 1 has high birth and death rates. Most HICs are in stage 4.

steps.answerWhy: Most HICs are in stage 4: low birth and death rates.

steps.question: Quiz, question 4 of 6: which is a historical cause of uneven development?
steps.right: Yes: colonialism comes from the past.

wrong.w1: Not quite: drought is physical. Colonialism is historical.
wrong.w2: Not quite: that is economic. Colonialism is historical.

steps.question: Quiz, question 5 of 6: which strategy gives very small loans to start a business?

wrong.w1: Not quite: debt relief cancels money owed. Microfinance gives small loans.
wrong.w2: Not quite: Fairtrade pays farmers a fair price. Microfinance gives small loans.

steps.answerWhy: Microfinance gives very small loans to start a business.

steps.question: Quiz, question 6 of 6: why can GNI per head mislead?

options.text: It is an average that hides inequality

steps.right: Yes: an average hides how unequally money is shared.

wrong.other: Not quite: it is an average that hides inequality.
wrong.w1: Not quite: it is measured for nearly every country. It misleads because it is an average that hides inequality.
wrong.w2: Not quite: it is all about money. It misleads because it is an average that hides inequality.

steps.answerWhy: GNI per head is an average, so it hides inequality.
